key_insight: Using central-Hermite moments for both sensing and collision makes a D3Q125 scheme far more frame-robust, largely eliminating boost-induced cross-order contamination in collision.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical path to more reliable kinetic solvers for translating or moving flows, especially where preserving moment order and positivity matters.
method: Compare three schemes: raw/raw (A), central/raw (B), and central/central (C).
Use a D3Q125 kinetic model with order-resolved log-Gaussian relaxation.
Test homogeneous translated perturbations and transport/collision frame discrepancy across a grid-CFL-boost matrix.
evidence_signal: In translated second-order tests, model C preserved third- and fourth-order modal purity to machine precision and cut total relative L-infinity collision frame discrepancy versus A by 65.342–98.102% (median 81.131%).
watch_item: The gain is partly configuration-dependent because transport continually re-injects frame error, so this moment-space improvement does not automatically translate to reduced macroscopic Galilean transport error.
paper_title: Central-Hermite Sensing and Collision for Frame-Robust Order-Resolved Relaxation on D3Q125
